## 0.5.10

- Style by app finds icons for installed apps before they run and keeps Store logos after use. App rows show plain names, with process names available to screen readers instead of visible subtitles.
- History checks saved audio once per row when refreshing the list. Recordings finishing in the background remain playable.
- Style by app keeps its controls in place when an app refresh has no changes. Holding a Back shortcut returns only one page.
- Dicta now needs sustained sound before treating a call app as heard. Once heard, quiet parts of the call do not bring back recording from every output.
- A newly recordable call app ends the fallback after one device check. If it fails before settling and no other call app is recording, Dicta records every output while retrying.
- Call apps that were working keep retrying when Windows audio briefly stops. Restarted apps reconnect their audio, and an app is recorded once even when its parts start together.
- Unrelated settings saves leave manual speaker-model downloads running, and turning Separate speakers back on quickly restarts a cancelled download. Separation still runs if its summary request cannot be saved; automatic summary requests older than a day expire.
- Meeting mute recovery keeps the next complete mute change after an interrupted journal write.
- Quickly starting and stopping another meeting gives its hidden indicator windows the full ten seconds before closing.
- Full cleanup catches more meaning changes when a rewrite drops a negative word and quietly uses local cleanup instead. It also keeps word-for-word retractions with unchanged internal punctuation, comma-interrupted negatives and repeated "I mean" restarts.
- Full cleanup keeps a real question's question mark when it removes a filler tag, while commands stay statements.
- After separating speakers again, uncertain name matches go to Names not kept, including when mixed speech joins another voice. A clear name match can survive absorbing an unnamed fragment under 20% of the new voice.
- When speaker recovery data is damaged, retyping a hidden call name reports that it could not be saved. The repair offer says "Speaker data couldn't be read."
- Quit gives pending audio one extra second to save incomplete markers, helping Re-transcribe avoid replacing a transcript with a shorter one.
- Meeting gap labels are retried when they cannot be saved, while recording continues. Pending labels are saved when recording stops, or noted in the log if they still cannot be.
- Meeting summaries receive the local date, title, your name when already known, meeting kind and duration, plus a reminder that transcription and automatic speaker labels may be wrong.
- No capitals or punctuation keeps spoken punctuation beside its words in very long dictations, including when cleanup changes words in the middle.
- History and the per-app list show each app's real icon instead of a letter.
- History now also keeps the words as first heard, before cleanup, for as long as it keeps the audio, to help track down cleanup mistakes. This stays on your computer.
- When part of a long dictation's rewrite is rejected, Dicta now keeps the cleaned text for the rest instead of falling back for all of it.
- Long dictations no longer get a stray period or capital letter in the middle of a sentence where the recording was split.
- Cleanup keeps "I feel like" and "he was like", and adds the missing space before a dollar amount.
- A new Dictation setting keeps the microphone ready for a minute after each dictation, so the first word is not cut off when you dictate again quickly. It is off by default because the microphone indicator stays on during that minute.
